Judgment:
Da vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc.

1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(Pfa Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provis
ions of the PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 2-5-2001 at about 6.30 PM Food Inspector B.P.Saroha purchased a sample of 'Guava Juice Drink' a food article for analysis from the accused No. 1 Sh.Vishwa Nath Da vs Vishwa Nath Batra Etc.

1 Batra at M/s Chefair The Pastry Shop, 13, Bengalow Road, Kamala Nagar, Delhi where the said food article was found stored for sale and the accused No.1 Sh.Vishwa Nath Batra was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling.
The sample consisted of 6x250 ml sealed tin cane of Guava Juice Drink taken as such in originally sealed condition bearing identical label declaration.

The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh.Arun Mishra,
SDM/LHA.
Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to PFA Act and Rules.
The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles.
Notice was given to accused No. 1 Sh.Vishwa Nath Batra and the price of the sample was also given to him.
Panchnama was prepared at the spot.

All the documents prepared by FI B.P.
Singh
were signed by accused No. 1 Vishwa Nath Batra and the other witness Sh.S.P. Singh, Fl.
Before starting sample proceedings efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward.
3. It is further stated that one counter-part of the sample was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition.
Public Analyst analysed DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. the sample and found the sample to be misbranded.

sentences.text:
The report of the Public Analyst is as follows :
"The sample is misbranded because the nature declared as Guava Juice Drink is misleading (fruit juice and fruit drink have different standards) further there is violation of rule 32 e, f and i."
4.

It is the case of the complainant that accused No. 1 Vishwa Nath Batra was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Chefair The Pastry Shop, 13, Bengalow Road, Kamala Nagar, Delhi at the time of sampling and the vendor disclosed that he had purchased the sampled commodity from M/s Gee Ess Overseas, D-S, Malka Ganj, Delhi.

It is further stated that M/s Gee Ess Overseas is a proprietorship firm and accused No. 2 Sh. Rajeev Kumar Sahni is the proprietor of the said firm and found to be incharge of and responsible for the day to day conduct of business of the said firm.

5. It is further stated that after conclusion of the investigation the entire case file including the statutory documents and PA's report and the FI's report were sent to the Director, PFA, Govt. of Delhi who had accorded Consent under section 20 of the PFA Act for instituting the case.

After obtaining the Consent of Director PFA, the present case was filed before the Court on 29.08.2001 alleging violation of section 2(ia)
(ix)(g)(k) of PFA Act read with rule 32 (e)(f)(i) pf PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16 of PFA Act.

6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. persons were summoned vide order dated 29.08.2001.

sentences.text: During the trial accused no. 1 has passed away.
7. At the trial, the prosecution examined three witness in support of its case.

PW-1 SDM/LHA Arun Mishra, PW-2 FI B.P. Saroha and PW-3 FI S.P. Singh deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 02.05.2001 and narrated the steps undertaken by him during the sample proceedings,
including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 6x250 ml can of Guava Juice Drink in original sealed condition, dividing it in three parts by considering two packets as one counterpart, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witness.

They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, notice in Form VI Ex. PW-1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, notice u/s 14 A Ex.PW1/D, counter parts of sample deposited vide receipt Ex.PW1/E & PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/F,
PA report Ex. PW-1/G.
After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/H was taken from the Director PFA and on the complaint Ex. PW-1/I was filed in the Court by PW-1.

A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex.PW1/J was sent to the accused persons vide registration receipt Ex.PW1/K.

sentences.text: Statements of the accused no. 1 & 2 under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 09.06.2010 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
They chose to lead evidence in their defence.
9. In their defence, the accused No. 1 Vishwa Nath Batra examined himself as DW-1.
Thereafter, vide order dated 30.05.2016 the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
10. I have heard the arguments advanced by Ld. Counsel for the complainant and Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused persons and have carefully perused the material available on record.
11. In a criminal case, the burden is only on the prosecution to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt by leading positive evidence.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and it has to be necessary discharged by the prosecution itself.
12. The case against the accused is that of misbranding.
The sample product in question is a Guava Juice Drink.

The case is based upon the report of public Analyst who has given the opinion that the sample is misbranded because the nature declared as Guava Juice Drink is misleading (Fruit Juice and Fruit Drink have different standards).
Further, there is a violation of Rule 32 (e), (f) & (i).
13. I have gone through Form VI, which has reproduced the label.
The date of manufacturing although does not seems to be written on the label but the date of expiry of the product was mentioned.

Although, a DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. customer will not be mislead at least to the extent that he will be aware of the shelf life of the product but since Rule 32 (f) mandates the mentioning of date of manufacturing, technically the offence of misbranding as far as not writing the date of manufacture is concerned, is established.

Rule 32 (e) has been declared by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India as ultra virus in Dwarka Nath vs Delhi Municipality, AIR 1971 Supreme Court 1844 and as far as Rule 32 (i) is concern, since the expiry date was mentioned, therefore, simply not mentioning the date when the product was best before, will not be misleading.

sentences.text: 15. Therefore, only the violation of Rule 32 (f) is established in the present case.
16. Now here we have two accused.

Accused no.1 Sh. Vishwa Nath Batra who was the vendor, who was selling the misbranded food article on the date of sale and he has not disputed this fact in his examination under section 313 Cr.PC and has admitted the same on Form VI Ex.PW1/B.
He has further examined himself as a defence witness and his only defence is that the Guava Juice was purchased by him from accused No. 2.
Now the question remains to be answered is that
whether accused No. 1 or whether accused No. 2 is liable for the offence of misbranding.

The accused No. 2 will be liable only if the accused No. 1 will be above to prove the warranty as contemplated u/s 19 (2)
of the PFA Act.
The accused No. 1 has placed on record a bill Ex.DW1/C1 although during his cross examination by State.
But he was unable to answer that who had issued the bill to him.
The prime DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. responsibility of selling the misbranded food item is upon accused no.1.

entities.text: prime DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 19 of PFA Act categorically provides that it shall be no defence in a prosecution for an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food to allege merely that the vendor was ignorant of the nature, substance or quality of food sold by him.

The vendor,
however, can escape his liability under the provision of Section 19(2) of PFA Act which provides as under :
"19.(2)) A vendor shall not be deemed to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food if he proves- (a) that he purchased the article of food - (i) in a case where a licence is prescribed for the sale thereof, from a duly licensed manufacturer distributor or dealer;
(ii) in any other case from any manufacturer, distributor or dealer, with a written warrantee in the prescribed form; and (b) That the article of food while in his possession was properly stored and that he sold it in the same state as he purchased it.
Rule 12-A of the Rules reads thus:
"12-A. Warranty. - Every manufacturer distributor or dealer selling an article of food to a vendor shall give either separately or in the bill, cash memo or label, a warranty in Form VI-A,"

4 17.
The accused No. 1 had given an undertaking on Form VI Ex. PW-1/B that he has purchased the juice from accused no.2 and he will provides bill.
The accused No. 1 has however not provided the bill to the complainant and has brought the same only at the fag DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc. end of the trial.

entities.text: DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. I have gone through the bill.
The accused No. 1 has failed to prove that who had issued the bill.

Further the name of the shop of accused No. 1 is M/s Chefair The Pastry Shop, whereas the bill shows the name of the shop as Cash C Chefair The Shop and further there is no address of this shop.
Further, there are no details of the product i.e. the juice supplied is Guava Juice.
Since the bill was not supplied during the investigation to the complainant, there is no investigation on this aspect that whether accused No. 1 has purchased the Guava Juice from accused No. 2.
Therefore, its not possible to connect the accused No. 2 with this bill and therefore the accused No. 2 cannot be convicted for the offence of misbranding.
The accused No. 1 has passed away during the trial and his death certificate is on record.

The liability in the present case for misbranding is that of accused No.
1.
But considering his death, the trial against him stand abated.
Accused No. 2 stands acquitted on the basis of aforesaid discussion.
Announced in the open court this 08th day of December 2017 SAMAR VISHAL ACMM-II (New Delhi), PHC DA vs Vishwa Nath Batra etc.
